_note: Trend check: hot specialisms, and the broader degrees that lead to them while keeping other doors open. CURATED DEMO: 'heat' is a qualitative note, not a measurement. Real job-advert demand data (for example Lightcast) is not connected yet. The 'doors' for each broader degree ARE computed from our own careers data.

specialisms.name: Quantum technologies
specialisms.buzz: Large public and private investment, and a lot of headlines.
specialisms.reality: Most jobs today are in research labs and a small number of specialist firms, and many roles want a Masters or PhD.

specialist.name: Quantum technologies degree
specialist.level: Mostly Masters or PhD; few undergraduate courses
specialist.doors: Narrow: research roles and a handful of specialist employers.

safer.subject: Mathematics
safer.why: Quantum computing is applied linear algebra and probability.

specialisms.fade: If the trend cools, Maths or Physics still lead to data, finance, engineering, software and teaching.
how: Study Maths, Physics or Computer science.
Choose quantum modules or a final-year project.
Join the physics or computing society and any quantum reading group.
Add a specialist Masters or PhD only once you're sure.

specialisms.name: Artificial intelligence
specialisms.buzz: Every industry is talking about it, and AI-specific courses have multiplied.
specialisms.reality: Employers still hire mostly for strong maths, programming and data skills that AI sits on top of, and the tools change fast.

specialist.name: Artificial intelligence degree
specialist.level: Undergraduate and Masters courses exist; many are new
specialist.doors: Narrower than the broad degrees underneath it.

safer.subject: Statistics
safer.why: Data, uncertainty and testing, which AI work depends on.

specialisms.fade: If AI hype settles, Computer science, Maths and Statistics still lead to software, data, finance and research.
how: Study Computer science, Maths or Statistics.
Take machine-learning modules and build projects with real data.
Enter Kaggle competitions and hackathons.
Specialise with a Masters if research appeals.

specialisms.name: Cyber security
specialisms.buzz: Skills shortages are widely reported and employers actively recruit.
specialisms.reality: A specialist degree is respected, but a general computing degree plus security practice opens just as many security roles and more besides.

safer.subject: Computer science
safer.why: Security builds on networks, systems and programming.

specialisms.fade: If security hiring cools, Computer science still leads to software, data and IT roles.
how: Study Computer science.
Join the cyber or ethical-hacking society and a capture-the-flag team.
Choose security modules and a security final-year project.
Apply for CyberFirst schemes and security internships.

specialisms.name: Clean energy and hydrogen
specialisms.buzz: Net-zero targets are driving investment and jobs, especially in Scotland and the North.
specialisms.reality: Demand depends on government policy and investment cycles, which can shift.

specialist.name: Renewable energy engineering degree
specialist.doors: Narrower than the broad engineering degrees.

specialisms.fade: If energy policy shifts, these engineering and physics degrees still lead to manufacturing, defence, transport and research.
how: Study Electrical or Mechanical engineering, or Physics.
Pick energy-systems modules and a related project.
Join an engineering society and a Formula Student or similar team.
Look for placements with energy firms.

specialisms.name: Biotechnology and synthetic biology
specialisms.buzz: New therapies and lab-grown materials get plenty of attention.
specialisms.reality: Many roles need a Masters or PhD, and funding for start-ups is cyclical.

specialist.name: Biotechnology degree
specialist.doors: Narrower than the broad science degrees.

safer.subject: Biomedical sciences
safer.why: The core biology of health and disease.

safer.subject: Mathematics
safer.why: Computational biology and statistics are in demand.

specialisms.fade: If biotech funding cools, a biomedical science degree still leads to NHS and hospital labs, pharma and research.
how: Study Biomedical sciences.
Join the science society and enter iGEM if your university has a team.
Get a lab placement or summer project.
Add a specialist Masters if the field still appeals.
